faq.q: What is the salary of a Sales and Marketing Executive in Bangladesh?
faq.a: Circulars we found show roughly BDT 15,000-30,000 a month for entry level, BDT 30,000-65,000 for mid level, and BDT 100,000-250,000 for regional managers and sales heads. Many posts add commission, TA/DA and two festival bonuses. Many circulars say negotiable, so confirm in the actual circular. Checked 16 Nov 2026.

faq.q: Do I need a marketing degree to get a sales job?
faq.a: Not always. Many circulars welcome graduates from any discipline, and FMCG territory officer posts often say fresh graduates are welcome. BBA or Marketing helps for brand and digital roles, but communication, follow-up and proof of results matter most.

faq.q: Is a commission-only job a good idea?
faq.a: Be very careful. Commission-only offers shift all the risk to you. Ask for the full pay structure in writing, how and when commission is paid, and verify the company. Never pay a deposit or buy a starter kit to get a job.

faq.q: How do I recognise an MLM or job scam?
faq.a: Warning signs are a security deposit, a starter kit, targets to recruit other people, unrealistic income promises and pressure to decide fast. Bangladesh Bank warned the public against MLM schemes on 9 March 2025, and the Daily Star has documented firms that took deposits from job-seekers.

faq.q: Will AI replace sales and marketing jobs?
faq.a: AI is already used for drafts, targeting and reports, but selling still depends on trust and judgement. The US Bureau of Labor Statistics projects 7 percent growth for market research analysts and marketing specialists from 2025 to 2035, and little or no change for wholesale and manufacturing sales representatives. Learn analytics and use AI tools while checking their output.

faq.q: How can freshers get their first sales or marketing job?
faq.a: Apply for Territory Sales Officer, Sales Executive and Marketing Executive posts that welcome freshers, take free HubSpot or Google Skillshop courses, build a small campaign or sales project with real numbers, and tailor your CV to each circular. Never pay anyone for a job.

faq.q: Is digital marketing a good career in Bangladesh?
faq.a: Many circulars ask for Meta Ads, Google Ads and SEO, and e-commerce is growing, but pay varies widely from about Tk 8,000-20,000 at the low end to Tk 50,000-65,000 for experienced managers. Results you can show with numbers raise your pay fastest.

faq.q: Can I work abroad in sales and marketing?
faq.a: Yes, through skilled-worker routes, company transfers, export roles and remote work for foreign clients. Be careful with fake offers: never pay a fee or hand over a passport to an unverified person, and verify any agency with the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment and BMET.

body_md:
**By [Daloyar Hassan Shishir](https://www.dhshishir.com)** · Career consultant, founder of Career Solutions and HereWeGrow · Facts last checked: 16 November 2026

> **Quick answer:** A Sales and Marketing Executive in Bangladesh finds customers, sells products or services, builds dealer and client relationships, runs promotions and tracks results against targets. Entry pay in the circulars we found is roughly BDT 15,000-30,000 a month, mid-level BDT 30,000-65,000, and regional or national sales heads BDT 100,000-250,000. Many offers add commission, TA/DA and festival bonuses. The job is open to graduates from any subject, but it rewards proof of results, and it is the field where "commission-only", "security deposit" and MLM-style offers hide the most scams.

## Sales and Marketing Executive career at a glance

| Question | Short answer |
|---|---|
| Who hires? | FMCG and consumer-goods companies, pharma and healthcare distributors, real estate, logistics, e-commerce and fintech, telecom, IT firms, banks, training institutes and agencies |
| Job titles in circulars | Sales Executive, Marketing Executive, Executive / Senior Executive (Sales and Marketing), Territory Sales Officer, Territory Sales Manager, Digital Marketing Executive, Business Development Executive, Key Account Executive |
| Minimum education | Usually a bachelor's degree; BBA or MBA in Marketing preferred in many circulars, but many sales posts accept any discipline |
| Must-have skills | Communication, negotiation, follow-up, target discipline, Excel and CRM basics; for digital roles, Meta Ads, Google Ads, SEO and analytics |
| Typical conditions | Targets, field travel (TA/DA), irregular hours near month-end, and pay that may be part fixed, part commission |
| Key rule | A real job does not ask you to pay a deposit, buy stock, or recruit friends to earn your pay |
| Global demand | The US Bureau of Labor Statistics projects 7 percent growth for market research analysts and marketing specialists from 2025 to 2035, but little or no change for wholesale and manufacturing sales representatives |

## What does a sales and marketing executive do?

Sales is about winning and keeping customers; marketing is about making the product known, wanted and easy to buy. In Bangladesh many circulars combine both in one title. A typical executive prepares a call and visit plan, meets retailers, dealers or corporate buyers, presents the product, negotiates, closes orders, follows up on payment and delivery, updates a CRM or Excel tracker, reports to the sales head, and supports promotions such as discounts, displays and social media campaigns. One FMCG circular asks a territory officer to meet value and volume targets, manage primary orders and check secondary sales for accuracy. A digital marketing circular asks for Meta and Google Ads, SEO, content planning and campaign reports.

**A normal day:** morning team call and target check, visits to outlets or calls to leads, a demonstration or quotation, follow-up on pending payments, a short report to the manager, and an evening update of the tracker. Digital executives replace visits with ad dashboards, content calendars and lead lists.

> A good salesperson solves a customer's problem and keeps the relationship after the sale. (our working rule for new sales staff)

## Scope: where this career can take you

- **Field sales and distribution:** territory officers and managers covering retailers and distributors, the backbone of FMCG, telecom and pharma.
- **Corporate and B2B sales:** selling services, software, equipment and logistics to companies.
- **Key account management:** looking after a few large customers over years.
- **Digital marketing:** paid ads, SEO, social media, email and analytics for e-commerce, startups and agencies.
- **Brand and product marketing:** positioning, pricing, launches and market research.
- **Business development:** finding new markets, partners and deals.
- **Export and international marketing:** buyer relations for garments, leather, agro and IT services.
- **Sales operations and CRM:** forecasting, reports and tools, a growing path as AI tools spread.
- **Own business or consultancy:** an online shop, an agency, a distributorship or freelance marketing.

## Salary in Bangladesh (2026 ranges)

| Level | Typical experience | Monthly pay (BDT) | Visual |
|---|---|---|---|
| Entry | 0-2 years, Executive or Officer | 15,000 - 30,000 | ██ |
| Mid | 3-7 years, Senior Executive to Manager | 30,000 - 65,000 | ████ |
| Senior | Regional Sales Manager to Head of Sales | 100,000 - 250,000 | █████████ |

**How we got these ranges.** Many circulars say "negotiable", so we used those that show numbers. In 2026: CS Care advertised a Marketing Executive at Tk 25,000 a month; BacBon Limited advertised a Senior Sales Executive at Tk 25,000-30,000; AGS Quality Action advertised a target-driven Sales Executive at Tk 35,000-40,000 with TA, mobile bill, tour allowance, yearly review and two festival bonuses; an aquaculture-products company advertised a Senior Executive or Assistant Manager (Sales and Marketing) with a minimum fixed salary of Tk 20,000 that rises with sales performance; a real-estate firm advertised a Senior Marketing Executive at Tk 30,000-35,000 plus commission; TechBrigades advertised a Senior Sales and Marketing Executive at Tk 40,000-65,000 with quarterly performance bonus and two festival bonuses. For digital roles: 6amTech listed a Digital Marketer at Tk 30,000-40,000, Startise a Paid Media Executive at Tk 30,000-50,000, Clickless a Digital Marketing Specialist at Tk 40,000, and Bheuni a Digital Marketing Manager (five years) at Tk 50,000-65,000. For seniors, Akij Group advertised a Regional Sales Manager at Tk 100,000-125,000 and Rahul Group a Head of Sales at Tk 200,000-250,000.

Online listings also show Digital Marketing Executive posts at Tk 8,000-20,000, so the bottom of the market is lower than our entry range. We did not use Payscale or AI-estimated salary posts, because their figures are very wide and their sources unclear. These are ranges, not promises. Confirm in the actual circular.

### Who pays the most?

As a general pattern: small trading firms and agencies → local manufacturers and growing online businesses → large FMCG, pharma, telecom and multinational companies with structured incentive plans. Within a company, pay rises fastest for people who own a territory or a major account, close large deals, or run digital campaigns that can be measured in sales.

**Global comparison:** in the United States, the median pay was USD 72,080 a year for wholesale and manufacturing sales representatives (non-technical), USD 104,920 for technical and scientific products, USD 78,760 for market research analysts and marketing specialists, USD 148,270 for sales managers and USD 166,790 for marketing managers (May 2025, US Bureau of Labor Statistics). Living costs and markets are very different, so do not compare the numbers directly.

## Benefits beyond salary

- Commission or performance incentive on top of a fixed salary (check how it is calculated and paid, in writing).
- TA/DA, mobile bill and fuel or tour allowance for field staff.
- Two festival bonuses a year and a yearly salary review in many circulars.
- Quarterly or yearly performance bonus at some employers.
- Provident fund at some larger companies.
- Training, product knowledge and fast promotion for people who deliver.
- Contacts and market knowledge that help if you later start your own business.

## Top employers: Bangladesh and the world

**Bangladesh: examples seen in circulars or careers pages (alphabetical, not a ranking)**

| Sector | Examples |
|---|---|
| FMCG and consumer goods | Akij Group, BD Foods, Himalaya Wellness Bangladesh, Kohinoor Chemical Company, Rahul Group, Square Food and Beverage, Tasmia Cosmetics and Toiletries, Unilever Bangladesh |
| Health and distribution | Mutual Trading Company (consumer health brands) and other pharma and healthcare distributors |
| Technology, e-commerce and BPO | 6amTech, BacBon, Bikroy, Daraz, TechBrigades |
| Logistics and services | AGS Quality Action, FR Logistics, LPG Bazar |

Always check each employer's own site for current vacancies. This is not a quality rating.

**A fact worth knowing:** the Unilever Bangladesh Territory Manager circular says freshers are discouraged from applying for that backfill post, while many FMCG territory officer circulars say fresh graduates are welcome. Read the level of each circular before you apply.

**World:** every company that sells needs sales and marketing people. Multinationals, export firms and remote employers hire for these skills, and digital marketing can be done for clients abroad. Immigration and licensing rules differ by country, so read the rules for each route.

## Skills employers ask for

| Skill | Why it matters | Demand |
|---|---|---|
| Communication and negotiation | Core of every sales post | █████ |
| Target discipline and follow-up | Targets and reports drive pay | █████ |
| Product and market knowledge | Customers trust people who know the product | ████ |
| Excel, MS Office and CRM basics | Pipeline and sales reports | █████ |
| Digital marketing (Meta Ads, Google Ads, SEO) | Core of digital executive circulars | █████ |
| Analytics and reporting | Decisions based on conversion data | ████ |
| Distributor and retail management | Field and FMCG roles | ████ |
| Content and copywriting (Bangla and English) | Campaigns, offers, social media | ███ |
| AI tools for drafts and analysis | Some circulars now list AI content tasks | ███ |
| Ethics and honest selling | Trust, repeat business and legal safety | █████ |

*Demand bars are our reading of recent circulars, not a statistical survey.*

## Free ways to build these skills

- **HubSpot Academy:** free courses and certifications in inbound marketing, content marketing, digital marketing and sales ([academy.hubspot.com](https://academy.hubspot.com)).
- **Google Skillshop:** free learning for Google Ads and Google Analytics ([skillshop.withgoogle.com](https://skillshop.withgoogle.com)); check the current certification list there.
- **Semrush Academy:** free SEO and digital marketing courses ([semrush.com/academy](https://www.semrush.com/academy/)).
- **Coursera and Alison:** audit sales, negotiation and marketing courses for free ([coursera.org](https://www.coursera.org), [alison.com](https://alison.com)).
- **Muktopaath:** free national e-learning in Bangla ([muktopaath.gov.bd](https://muktopaath.gov.bd)).
- **Practice:** make a mock marketing plan for a real local brand, run a small campaign for a club, or sell for a friend's online page and record the results. Numbers on your CV beat adjectives.

## Qualifications, licences, scholarships and study support

| Step | Body | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| Bachelor's degree | University (BBA, Marketing, any discipline) | Most circulars ask for a bachelor's degree; Marketing or BBA is often preferred |
| MBA | Universities and business schools | Useful for brand, product and management tracks |
| Free certificates | HubSpot, Google Skillshop, Semrush | Good proof of skill; they do not replace results |
| Paid professional programmes | Marketing and sales bodies, institutes and bootcamps | Check accreditation, fees and job outcomes yourself before paying |
| Product training | Employers and brands | Often the most valuable in FMCG, pharma and telecom |

**Support to explore (check each official site for current rules):**

- **Chevening (UK):** [chevening.org](https://www.chevening.org) for a funded master's in marketing, business or management.
- **Commonwealth Scholarships:** [cscuk.fcdo.gov.uk](https://cscuk.fcdo.gov.uk).
- **DAAD (Germany):** [daad.de](https://www.daad.de/en/).
- **Fulbright (USA):** through the US Embassy in Dhaka.
- **University scholarships:** ask about merit and need-based awards for BBA and MBA.

> **Warning on sales job scams:** a real employer pays you for your work. Be very careful if an offer asks for a "security deposit" or "refundable deposit", asks you to buy products or a starter kit, pays only commission, or makes you recruit other people. The Daily Star has documented an MLM firm that took deposits from job-seekers and then set recruiting targets, and another that lured a student with a Tk 20,000 salary plus commission. Bangladesh Bank issued a public warning on 9 March 2025 against MLM schemes that promise unrealistic profits and pay referral-based commissions, and the MLM Activities (Control) Act 2013 regulates the sector. Online "task" jobs that promise Tk 200-1,500 per order and ask you to deposit money are also reported scams. Never pay for a job, an interview or a "training seat". For work abroad, verify any agency with the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment and BMET.

## Long-term career timeline

| Years | Typical title | What to master |
|---|---|---|
| 0-2 | Sales Executive / Territory Sales Officer / Marketing Executive | Product knowledge, visits and calls, follow-up, reports, one digital or CRM tool |
| 2-5 | Senior Executive | Hitting targets, handling a territory or key accounts, negotiation, simple analytics |
| 5-8 | Assistant Manager / Territory Sales Manager | Team supervision, distributor management, planning, budgets |
| 8-12 | Area, Regional or Brand Manager | Strategy, forecasting, pricing, managing managers |
| 12+ | Head of Sales / Marketing, Director or CEO track | Revenue ownership, market strategy, culture and ethics |

## Plan your own path (5-minute worksheet)

Copy these five lines and fill them in today:

1. **My level now:** (student / fresher / ___ years in sales or marketing)
2. **My target role in 3 years:** ___
3. **Three skills I lack** (use the checklist on this page): ___, ___, ___
4. **One learning step this year:** (HubSpot sales course / Google Ads / SEO / CRM / MBA)
5. **My weekly study hours and day:** ___ hours on ___

Then take the free skill test on this page and compare the result with line 3.

## Career shifts: where sales and marketing professionals move

- **Sales → key account or business development management.**
- **Sales → product or brand management.**
- **Marketing → digital marketing specialist, SEO or paid-media lead.**
- **Sales → sales operations, CRM and analytics.**
- **Sales or marketing → customer success or customer service leadership.**
- **Sales → procurement, trading or distribution business.**
- **Sales or marketing → own business, agency or freelance consultancy.**

## Where will you find more peace of mind?

We have no survey that ranks the calm of different sales jobs, so this is a general pattern. Field FMCG and commission-heavy jobs can mean travel, month-end target pressure and income that moves with sales, while B2B, key account and in-house marketing roles are often steadier, with longer cycles. Three habits protect your peace: understand exactly how your pay and targets are calculated before you accept, keep a cash buffer for months with low commission, and never promise a customer something you cannot deliver. Ask about fixed pay, target setting, TA/DA and payment dates in the interview, and get the answers in writing. If stress becomes heavy, talk to a mentor or a mental health professional.

## Faith and history: honest trade

**The Quran.** Al-Baqarah says Allah has permitted trade ([2:275 on quran.com](https://quran.com/2/275)), the basis for honest selling as a respected livelihood. An-Nisa instructs believers to trade by mutual consent ([4:29](https://quran.com/4/29)), a reminder that pressure and deception have no place in a sale. Al-Mutaffifin condemns those who give short measure ([83:1-3](https://quran.com/83/1)), a standard for accurate weights, honest descriptions and fair prices.

**Hadith.** The Prophet (peace be upon him) is reported to have said that the truthful, trustworthy merchant will be with the prophets, the truthful and the martyrs (reported in Jami at-Tirmidhi; check the grading before you quote it publicly).

**History.** Muhammad (peace be upon him) worked as a trader before prophethood and was known for honesty, and Khadijah (may Allah be pleased with her) was a successful businesswoman who employed him. Honest trade has deep roots in this region too: Bengal's rivers and ports connected it to markets across Asia for centuries. Sales and marketing carry that tradition forward.

## Your contribution to the nation

Sales and marketing professionals connect Bangladeshi producers with buyers. A territory officer puts food, medicine and household goods in rural shops, a digital marketer helps a small online business find customers, and an export marketer wins orders that create jobs. The Daily Ittefaq reported in March 2026 that active Facebook commerce page entrepreneurs are estimated at 200,000-250,000, and the Financial Express reports card-based e-commerce transactions averaging about Tk 21.85 billion a month between August 2025 and June 2026. Honest selling and accurate marketing also protect consumers and build trust in local brands.

## Your contribution to the world

Bangladeshi marketers support global brands, remote clients and export buyers, and help local products such as garments, leather, jute, food and software reach new markets. Truthful advertising, fair pricing and respect for customers are values that travel across borders.

## If you want to be an entrepreneur

- **Online shop or social commerce page** with a clear niche, honest descriptions and reliable delivery.
- **Digital marketing agency or freelance service** for small businesses (start with one or two clients and real results).
- **Distributorship or retail supply** built on the territory you already know.
- **Dealer or corporate sales agency** representing a few non-competing products.
- **Training and coaching** in sales, communication or social media for students and small shops.
- **Content and brand services** (copywriting, photos, video) for local brands.

Keep records, write clear agreements and register your business as the law requires. Stay away from anything that earns mainly from recruiting other people.

## Research opportunities

- Topics with real need in Bangladesh: social commerce and trust, digital payments and cash on delivery, consumer behaviour in rural markets, AI in digital marketing, retail distribution and last-mile selling, and women entrepreneurs online.
- Where to learn and publish: business schools, university journals and e-commerce research bodies. A university report, *Artificial Intelligence in Digital Marketing: A Bangladeshi Perspective* (United International University repository), is a useful starting point.
- Path: a final-year project → marketing or research executive → master's or PhD in marketing (the scholarships above fund many of these).

## Whom to follow and learn from

Follow organisations and practitioners who show methods and numbers: HubSpot Academy and Google Skillshop for skills, the e-Commerce Association of Bangladesh (e-CAB) for market news, The Daily Star's [Next Step](https://www.thedailystar.net/next-step) and The Business Standard for careers and business. On LinkedIn, follow sales heads and digital marketers who share campaigns and results, and ignore accounts that sell income promises or recruiting funnels.

## Where to find sales and marketing jobs

- [BDJobs](https://www.bdjobs.com) (search Sales Executive, Territory Sales Officer, Marketing Executive, Digital Marketing Executive, Business Development) and company career pages.
- Unilever's [careers site](https://careers.unilever.com), and the career pages of large FMCG, pharma and telecom firms.
- [Skill.jobs](https://skill.jobs), LinkedIn, university career centres and newspaper job pages.
- Bikroy lists many posts, but pay and quality vary widely, so check each company before you apply.
- Use official company pages or verified circulars only. Do not pay anyone for a job or an interview.

## Sales and Marketing CV: what to write

Your CV should show numbers: targets, sales, customers, campaigns and results.

| Weak line | Better line |
|---|---|
| Responsible for sales. | Achieved 108% of a Tk 12 lakh monthly target across 60 outlets in 3 months (use your real numbers). |
| Managed social media. | Grew a page from 2,000 to 9,000 followers and generated 140 leads with Tk 15,000 in Meta Ads (use your real numbers). |
| Good communication skills. | Presented to 25 dealers and closed 6 new accounts in one quarter. |

*Use only your real, provable details. Never exaggerate and never share a client's confidential data in your CV.*

**What to include:** a two-line summary, targets and results with numbers, territory or client types, tools (Excel, CRM, Meta Ads, Google Ads, SEO), certificates with dates, education, languages and a clear contact line.

**Career objective samples:**

- *Fresher:* "BBA graduate with a university marketing project, HubSpot certification and strong follow-up habits seeking a Sales Executive role to build customer relationships and meet targets."
- *Experienced:* "Territory Sales Officer with 3 years in FMCG distribution, consistently above target, seeking a Senior Executive role to manage a larger territory and team."

Build yours free with the HereWeGrow CV Builder and the Sales and Marketing CV template.

## Common mistakes in applications

- Not reading the circular to the end (fixed salary, commission rules, probation, travel).
- A CV full of duties but no targets, sales or campaign results.
- Accepting an offer with no written pay structure or with "commission only".
- Paying a deposit, buying stock or joining a "recruit and earn" scheme.
- Promising customers more than the product can do, or copying competitors' claims without proof.
- Ignoring Excel and follow-up discipline: missed follow-up is lost sales.

## Sources and method

Figures were checked on 16 November 2026 and will be reviewed regularly. Pay ranges combine the circulars that show salary and are estimates; senior ranges rest on only a few posts. Statistics from the US and e-commerce market estimates come from different sources and definitions, so treat them as indications, not exact numbers.

- US Bureau of Labor Statistics: [Wholesale and Manufacturing Sales Representatives](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/sales/wholesale-and-manufacturing-sales-representatives.htm); [Sales Managers](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/management/sales-managers.htm); [Market Research Analysts](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/Business-and-Financial/Market-research-analysts.htm); [Advertising, Promotions and Marketing Managers](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/management/advertising-promotions-and-marketing-managers.htm)
- Circulars and listings: [TechBrigades, Senior Sales and Marketing Executive (EWU notice)](https://www.ewubd.edu/notice-details/senior-sales-marketing-executive-june-2026-techbrigades-limited); [AGS Quality Action, Sales Executive](https://hotjobs1.bdjobs.com/ags-quality-action-limited/agsqal11.html); [Dailami Innovative Technology, Senior Marketing Executive](https://hotjobs1.bdjobs.com/dit-dailami-innovative-technology-/dit.html); [Akij Group, Regional Sales Manager](https://skill.jobs/jobs/regional-sales-manager-rsm-LZ2lPb3I); [Rahul Group, Head of Sales (TBS Jobs)](https://www.tbsnews.net/node/1483111); [6amTech, Digital Marketer](https://6amtech.com/digital-marketer/); [Startise, Paid Media Executive](https://easy.jobs/jobs-2/paid-media-executive/); [Bheuni, Digital Marketing Manager](https://bheuni.io/job/details/digital-marketing-manager); [Unilever, Territory Manager](https://careers.unilever.com/en/job/dacca/territory-manager/34155/97794862352); [Square Food and Beverage, Territory Sales Officer](https://brandpractitioners.com/?p=44458); [Bikroy, Digital Marketing Executive jobs](https://bikroy.com/jobs/digital-marketing-executive); circular posts on LinkedIn for [BacBon](https://bd.linkedin.com/in/amindu14), [CS Care](https://bd.linkedin.com/in/toriqul-islam123), [Clickless](https://bd.linkedin.com/in/tonmoy-baidya) and [FR Logistics](https://bd.linkedin.com/in/fuadarshad); an aquaculture-products circular on [JobConnectBD](https://jobconnectbd.blogspot.com/2026/01/job-title-senior-executive-assistant.html)
- E-commerce: The Daily Ittefaq: [EID online shopping gains momentum](https://en.ittefaq.com.bd/15747/eid-online-shopping-gains-momentum); The Financial Express: [From cash to cards, e-commerce shift gathers pace](https://thefinancialexpress.com.bd/trade/from-cash-to-cards-e-commerce-shift-gathers-pace); Dhaka Tribune: [The price puzzle in Bangladesh's booming online fashion market](https://www.dhakatribune.com/bangladesh/409462/the-price-puzzle-in-bangladesh%E2%80%99s-booming-online)
- AI and digital marketing: [Artificial Intelligence in Digital Marketing: A Bangladeshi Perspective (UIU)](https://dspace.uiu.ac.bd/items/24f843e3-2353-4525-b289-7572644f63a7); The Daily Star: [What skills are essential for digital marketers in Bangladesh?](https://images.thedailystar.net/node/3810531); NextJobz: [Bangladesh job market trends 2026](https://blog.nextjobz.com.bd/?p=633) (a job-site blog, so read as secondary)
- Free learning: [HubSpot Academy certifications (Coursera guide)](https://coursera.org/articles/hubspot-certification); [HubSpot Academy overview (Career Shifters)](https://www.careershifters.org/retraining-directory/marketing-and-communications/hubspot-academy)

growth_plan.y1: Learn the product and market, build follow-up and reporting habits, finish a free HubSpot or Google Skillshop course, and land a first Executive or Territory Officer role.
growth_plan.y2: Hit targets consistently, own a territory or key accounts, learn analytics and one digital channel, and use AI tools while checking their output.
growth_plan.y3: Move toward Senior Executive or Assistant Manager: lead a small team, manage distributors or campaigns, and choose a path in field sales, key accounts, brand or digital.

goal_sheet: Week 1-2: Pick a product or brand and write a one-page sales pitch and answers to five common objections
Week 3-4: Learn Excel basics and build a mock sales tracker with a pivot table
Month 2: Finish one free HubSpot Academy course and one Google Skillshop module
Month 3: Run a small real project, such as promoting a friend's page or a club event, and record the numbers
Month 4: Learn the basics of Meta Ads or SEO and create a mock campaign plan for a local brand
Month 5: Practise negotiation and cold-call scripts with a friend; learn CRM basics
Month 6: Update CV with results, apply to 10 circulars, practise 20 interview questions

test.q: A job offer says: pay a Tk 20,000 refundable deposit to start, then earn by bringing in more recruits. What should you do?
options: Refuse; deposits and recruit-to-earn plans are common scam and MLM warning signs
test.explain: Real employers pay you; deposits and recruiting targets are classic warning signs reported by The Daily Star and Bangladesh Bank.

test.q: What is the best first step before visiting a new retailer?
options: Check past orders, set a clear goal for the visit and prepare the offer
test.explain: Preparation and a clear goal make visits productive and repeatable.

test.q: A customer says your price is too high. What is the best response?
options: Ask what they compare it with, explain the value and offer options
test.explain: Understand the objection first; discount only when the value case has been made.

test.q: Which Excel tool best summarises sales by region and product?
test.explain: PivotTables summarise large sales tables quickly for reports.

test.q: What does CRM software mainly help a salesperson do?
options: Track leads, contacts and follow-ups in one place
test.explain: A CRM keeps your pipeline organised so no lead is forgotten.

test.q: A Facebook ad gets many clicks but no sales. What should you check first?
options: The landing page, offer, price and targeting, using the analytics data
test.explain: Clicks without sales point to a problem after the click; use data to find where people drop off.

options: The share of people who take the wanted action, such as buying
test.explain: Conversion rate = people who act divided by people who visited or clicked.

test.q: Why is accurate product description important in marketing?
options: False claims lose trust, create returns and can break consumer rules
It only matters for big firms
test.explain: Honest descriptions protect trust and reduce complaints and legal risk.

test.q: Your commission is paid on collected payments, not orders. What should you do?
options: Follow up on payment dates and track dues
Ask the customer to pay you personally
test.explain: If pay depends on collection, tracking dues is part of the job.

test.q: An agency offers a 'sales job' that pays only commission and asks you to buy a starter kit. This is:
options: A warning sign; ask for the pay structure in writing and verify the company before paying anything
test.explain: Starter-kit and commission-only models often shift the risk to you; verify and do not pay.

test.q: An AI tool writes your ad copy. What is the responsible approach?
options: Check facts, prices, tone and claims before publishing and keep your judgement
Hide that you used it from your manager
test.explain: AI speeds drafts but you are responsible for accuracy and honesty.

test.q: Which result best shows your value on a CV?
options: Achieved 110% of a monthly target across 50 outlets
test.explain: Specific numbers prove results; adjectives do not.

cv_template_notes: Use the HWG Sales and Marketing CV (clean, one-column layout). Start with a two-line summary, then targets and results with numbers, territory or client types, tools used (Excel, CRM, Meta Ads, Google Ads, SEO), certificates with dates, education and languages. Keep it to 1 page for freshers and 2 pages at most. Use only provable details, never share confidential client data, and never invent numbers. File name: YourName_SalesMarketing_CV.pdf.
cover_letter_md:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am applying for the Sales Executive position advertised on [site/date]. I hold a [degree] from [university] and have [internship/work] experience in [sales/marketing]. In my [role/project] I [one provable detail, e.g. achieved 108% of a monthly target across 60 outlets or generated 140 leads with a Tk 15,000 ad budget].

I follow up carefully, keep honest records, and I am comfortable with targets and travel. I would be glad to contribute to [Company name] and to keep growing in your sales team.

I have attached my CV and would welcome an interview.

Sincerely,
[Your name]
[Phone] | [Email]
interview_qs: Tell me about yourself. (Tip: 45 seconds: education, one sales or marketing experience with a number, why this company.)
Why do you want to work in sales and marketing? (Tip: Give a real reason such as relationships, targets and results; avoid just 'I like talking'.)
Sell me this pen. (Tip: Ask about my needs first, then link features to benefits and close politely.)
How do you plan a day of field visits? (Tip: Route, priority outlets, goals, stock and follow-ups.)
How do you handle a customer who says your price is too high? (Tip: Ask questions, show value, offer options and avoid blind discounts.)
Tell me about a target you missed and what you learned. (Tip: Be honest, show analysis and the fix.)
Tell me about a target you exceeded. (Tip: Give numbers and what you did differently.)
How do you follow up with a lead that has gone quiet? (Tip: Short, useful messages at planned intervals.)
What is the difference between sales and marketing? (Tip: Marketing creates demand and awareness; sales converts it into orders.)
How do you manage a distributor who is late on payment? (Tip: Facts, relationship, written reminders and escalation.)
What is a sales funnel? (Tip: Awareness, interest, decision, purchase, repeat; give an example.)
How do you use Excel in sales work? (Tip: Trackers, pivot tables, targets versus achievement.)
What CRM or sales tools have you used? (Tip: Answer honestly and describe what you actually did.)
How would you promote a new product with a small budget? (Tip: Target audience, channels, offer, measure and adjust.)
What is the difference between SEO and paid ads? (Tip: Organic ranking over time versus paid visibility now.)
How do you measure the success of a Facebook ad campaign? (Tip: Reach, clicks, leads, cost per lead, conversion and sales.)
What is conversion rate and how can you improve it? (Tip: Landing page, offer, speed, trust signals, follow-up.)
How do you do market research on a small budget? (Tip: Shop visits, customer surveys, competitor pages, free analytics.)
How do you decide a price for a product? (Tip: Cost, competitors, value and margin.)
What would you do in your first 30 days in this role? (Tip: Learn the product, customers and tools, and set targets with your manager.)
How do you handle rejection? (Tip: Learn from it, ask for feedback and keep the relationship.)
How would you use AI tools in your work? (Tip: Be honest: drafts and analysis, then check facts and claims.)
A customer asks you to exaggerate a product's benefits. What do you do? (Tip: Stay honest and explain the real benefits.)
A recruiter offers a job after you pay a deposit. What do you do? (Tip: Refuse, verify the company and report it.)
How do you handle a competitor who is cheaper? (Tip: Focus on value, service and relationships rather than price alone.)
Tell me about a time you worked with a difficult teammate or customer. (Tip: Show calm, respect and outcome.)
Are you comfortable with travel and target pressure? (Tip: Answer honestly and ask about TA/DA and territory size.)
What are your salary expectations? (Tip: Give a range based on the circular and market; ask how fixed pay and commission are split.)
Where do you see yourself in five years? (Tip: Name a role such as territory manager, brand manager or digital lead and the steps you are taking.)
Do you have any questions for us? (Tip: Ask about targets, training, territory, incentive plan and growth.)
